subject: Business
title: Mentorship: Growing the Next Generation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Mentorship: Growing the Next Generation.

hook.text: Bill Campbell mentored Steve Jobs, Eric Schmidt, and Jeff Bezos. He never ran a tech company himself.

buildup.text: Mentorship transfers wisdom that can't be learned from books: judgment, perspective, and emotional intelligence.

discovery.text: Great mentors don't give answers. They ask questions that help the mentee find their own.

twist.text: Mentoring benefits the mentor too. Teaching forces reflection. Helping others grow deepens your own understanding.

climax.text: Companies with formal mentoring programs have 72% higher retention rates, per a Sun Microsystems study.

punchline.text: A leader's greatest legacy is the leaders they create.

quiz.question: What is the primary benefit of great mentorship?
options: It transfers judgment and perspective that can't be learned from books
It gives mentees step-by-step instructions for success
It guarantees promotions for the mentee

details.summary: Mentorship pairs experienced leaders with emerging talent to accelerate professional development through guidance, advice, and shared experience. Effective mentors do not give all the answers but ask powerful questions that help mentees develop their own judgment and capability.
details.whyItMatters: Mentorship multiplies leadership capacity across the organization. Leaders who invest in developing others create a pipeline of capable talent that ensures organizational continuity and builds loyalty among high-potential employees.
takeaways: Effective mentors ask powerful questions rather than providing all the answers
Mentorship develops judgment that cannot be learned from books or training alone
Organizations with strong mentorship cultures retain top talent longer

faq.question: What makes a great mentor versus a mediocre one?
faq.answer: Great mentors listen more than they talk, share failures alongside successes, ask questions that develop the mentee's own thinking, customize advice to individual circumstances, and maintain consistent availability. Mediocre mentors lecture from their experience without adapting to the mentee.

faq.question: How should a mentee maximize the value of a mentorship relationship?
faq.answer: Come prepared with specific questions or challenges. Follow through on commitments made during conversations. Be open to uncomfortable feedback. Share updates on how advice was applied and what happened. Respect the mentor's time. Take responsibility for driving the relationship forward.
